_comment: Index lifecycle for honeypot-events. ROLLOVER ONLY -- there is deliberately
no delete phase, and adding one is a decision, not a tidy-up.
Captured attacker telemetry is this project's research data and a delete
phase is irreversible: it runs on a timer, against data nobody is watching,
and the first sign it was wrong is a gap in a paper. What this policy buys
instead is that no single index grows without bound, so old indices become
individually droppable BY HAND once you have decided you do not need them.
Disk still fills eventually -- slowly, and visibly in _cat/indices.
max_primary_shard_size over max_size because it is the one that tracks what
actually degrades: a shard past ~50gb is slow to search and slow to
relocate. 5gb is conservative for a single-node cluster with a 1gb heap
max_age caps how long a single index stays open for writes even on a quiet
honeypot, so a VPS collecting a trickle still produces separable indices
rather than one index spanning a year.
No warm or cold phase: this is a single-node cluster with number_of_replicas
0, so there is no second tier to move anything to. forcemerge and
set_priority would be motion without effect.
